precepts.text: Nehemiah contended that the house of God was forsaken, gathered the tithe of corn, wine, and oil into the treasuries, set faithful treasurers, and prayed, wipe not out my good deeds. The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings brought to the house.
precepts.point: You cannot boast in sacrificing as though it makes you special, because it is done; Christ died for us. Justification is through Christ, and it is in the same chapter as let God be true and every man a liar.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
“Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” What are the deeds of the law? Nehemiah shows them: “Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.” We are talking about the house of God.

“Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.” This is what they brought: the offerings. He “made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah”, “for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren.”

“Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.” The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings he brought to the house of God.

And it is in the same chapter of Romans where God is justified in his sayings and overcomes when he is judged: let God be true, and every man a liar. This is serious. Your salvation is at hand, and a teacher who is up at the podium drinking, talking about sex and baby oil and prostitution, instead of instructing the people what these scriptures are talking about, is not a leader to lead people to God. He is a joke.

precepts.text: Remember me, O my God, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for the offices thereof. Nehemiah calls his deeds what they were.
precepts.point: Never let a Christian confound you in these verses. They do not know the Bible; we do.

precepts.text: Jews married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children could not speak in the Jews' language.
precepts.point: In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.”

These are the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations, the bastard the law shuts out of the congregation to his tenth generation, and Ashdod is the very city Zechariah named for the bastard to dwell in, a city given to Judah and lost.

Why did the children speak half in the speech of Ashdod and not the Jews' language? Because the mothers do the raising of the children. A wife of Ashdod raises children that speak Ashdod.

precepts.text: When they read that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.
precepts.point: In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever”. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses: “On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever; Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.”

And when they heard the law, “they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.” Our people had intermarried with the mixed multitude and had children with them, and hearing this law they separated them from Israel. The law still had the same force in Nehemiah's day that it had in Moses': for ever.

precepts.text: Nehemiah said, if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you; the same spirit and speech is in our people to this day.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you.” I will lay hands on you: that is how Nehemiah talked, and that is how we talk. The same spirit and speech is in our people to this day.

It is the same with the avenger of blood whose heart is hot: heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated. Our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way we do.

precepts.text: Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and Ruth was of Moab; their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews' language.
precepts.point: Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive in Israel, and although she was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel.

note.label: Ruth 4: Boaz Redeems the Inheritance

precepts.why:
Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Nehemiah shows what happens when it is. “In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.”

Ruth was of Moab. A child's first teacher is the mother: she nurses him, he spends all his time with her, and he takes on her ways. So the children of those wives could not even speak the Jews' language. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive and was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it immediately after it was born and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel. That is why the neighbours said, There is a son born to Naomi.

precepts.text: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, the history behind why the Ammonite and Moabite were shut out of the congregation.
precepts.point: When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
The law read that day said the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever because they “hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them”. This is that history. Balak “sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor”, saying, “Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me”.

Balak wanted Israel cursed so he could smite them and drive them out of the land, “for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.” Hiring Balaam to curse Israel is why the Ammonite and Moabite were shut out of the congregation, and as Nehemiah says, “our God turned the curse into a blessing.”

precepts.text: The law itself: an Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the Lord for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water and hired Balaam against them.
precepts.point: When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
This is what they found written in the book of Moses: “An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever: Because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.”

The law itself gives both reasons Nehemiah repeats: they met not Israel with bread and water when they came out of Egypt, and they hired Balaam to curse them. When the people heard this law, “they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.” The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off.

precepts.text: The commandment to remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy and do no work, which the Sabbath commerce directly transgressed.
precepts.point: He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Nehemiah saw men treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and carrying wine, grapes, figs and all manner of burdens into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and ware to the children of Judah. This is the commandment they transgressed: “Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates”.

Six days for labour, the seventh for the Lord, and no work in it, not even by the cattle or the stranger within the gates. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment, which is why Nehemiah contended with the nobles of Judah: “What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?” Their fathers did this, the Most High brought all this evil upon the city for it, and now they were bringing more wrath upon Israel.

precepts.text: The Most High commanded to bear no burden on the Sabbath day nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem, the very burdens Nehemiah shut the gates against.
precepts.point: He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
The burdens Nehemiah saw brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath were the very thing the Most High had warned about through Jeremiah: “Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem; Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.”

No burden on the Sabbath day, and none brought in by the gates of Jerusalem. That is exactly what the men of Judah were doing with their sheaves and asses and wine, and what the men of Tyre were doing with their fish and ware, and these are the very burdens Nehemiah shut the gates against. “Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city?” Jeremiah's warning to the fathers had gone unheeded, and Nehemiah would not let it be repeated.

precepts.text: The law forbids marrying the nations because they will turn the son away from following the Most High to serve other gods, and kindle his anger to destroy them.
precepts.point: Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and their children “spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language”. The law forbade this from the beginning: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.”

The reason is given in the law: they will turn the son away from following the Most High to serve other gods, and his anger will be kindled to destroy them suddenly. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law, the very turning away the law warned of. That is why Nehemiah made them swear, “Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons”.

precepts.text: Solomon loved many strange women, and when he was old his wives turned away his heart after other gods, exactly as the law warned they would.
precepts.point: Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Nehemiah asked, “Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things?” Here is the record: “But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites; Of the nations concerning which the Lord said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.”

He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and “when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.” Exactly as the law warned, the strange women turned away his heart.

Among many nations there was no king like Solomon, beloved of his God, and even him did outlandish women cause to sin. If it happened to him, the men of Judah marrying wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab had no ground to think it would not happen to them.

precepts.text: Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall; no one is above the temptation that took Solomon down.
precepts.point: Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Solomon, beloved of his God and made king over all Israel, was still caused to sin by outlandish women. Paul's warning follows from that: “Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.”

No one is above the temptation that took Solomon down. The Jews Nehemiah contended with had thought themselves able to marry strange wives without harm, and their children could not even speak the Jews' language. Let him that thinks he stands take heed.

precepts.text: No man can come to the Most High except the Father draw him, and he draws him when he hears the words of this Bible, which is why the sheep hear his voice and a stranger they will not follow.
precepts.point: Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Nehemiah chased away the son of Joiada who was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, because the priesthood and its covenant had been defiled, and “Thus cleansed I them from all strangers”. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are.

Christ says, “No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.” No man can come to the Most High except the Father draw him, and he draws him when he hears the words of this Bible. That is why the sheep hear his voice and a stranger they will not follow.

The strangers Nehemiah cleansed out had no part in the covenant of the priesthood. Those who are drawn by the Father hear these words and know their own history in them, and it is those he will raise up at the last day. Nehemiah closes his book asking, “Remember me, O my God, for good.”

precepts.text: The jews had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and even Solomon was caused to sin by outlandish women; strange wives are women of the other nations.
precepts.point: The ways of a man are before the eyes of the Most High and He ponders all his goings. The wicked man's own iniquities take him and he is held with the cords of his sins, dying without instruction in the greatness of his folly.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?” The strange woman carries a double meaning: a woman of another nation, and a woman outside of your own wife. Nehemiah shows the first.

“In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.” The jews had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and their children could not even speak the language. Nehemiah “contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.”

Then he brings Solomon himself: “Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin.” Even Solomon was caused to sin by outlandish women. Strange wives are women of the other nations, and the man who embraces the bosom of a stranger is held with the cords of his sins.

precepts.text: Bearing burdens, treading winepresses, and selling on the sabbath was the labor forbidden, none of which is what Christ or the disciples did.
precepts.point: They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Nehemiah shows the labor that was actually forbidden: “In those days saw I in Judah some treading wine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals.”

Treading winepresses, bearing burdens and selling on the Sabbath is occupational labor. None of that is what Christ or the disciples did. The charge against them was envy, because they gathered and unified the people.
